To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
summer pruning techniques are useful to control the ripening of white wine grapes.

1) basal leaf removal (BLR) at pre-flowering (ELR) and bunch thinning (50% crop removed at lag phase) (BT) are effective to increase grape soluble solid content and reduce yield per vine, 2) ELR, but not BT, is effective to maintain the desired titratable acidity, 3) ELR is more effective than BT in increasing the ratio between soluble solids and titratable acidity.
the use of summer pruning in the Ortrugo cultivar can lead to an increase of the grape sugar content and to a decrease in the yield per plant, without affecting the acidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of summer pruning as an innovative and sustainable technique to manage vine performance and grape ripening.
the effects of summer pruning and bunch thinning on yield and grape compositional patterns in the white V. vinifera cv Ortrugo.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of summer pruning is an efficient way to pilot grape composition in white Vitis viniferawine production.
the best summer pruning technique for Ortrugo is ELR, as it is able to maintain the optimal TA and to increase the total soluble solids at the same time.
summer pruning is a tool to pilot grape ripening towards desired composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
summer pruning techniques can be applied to Ortrugo to increase sugar accumulation rate, thus allowing for a slight anticipation of harvest date.
summer pruning is not a panacea, but it is an effective way to pilot ripening, especially in the context of global warming.
the timing of summer pruning is a key factor in determining the final composition of the crop, as it can affect the rate of sugar accumulation and, to a lesser extent, TA.
